questions.text: The number of relations, defined on the set $\{a, b, c, d\}$, which are both reflexive and symmetric, is equal to :
questions.sol:
A reflexive relation must contain all 4 pairs $(x,x)$.
Symmetry means the off-diagonal pairs come in pairs $\{(x,y),(y,x)\}$; there are $\binom{4}{2}=6$ such pairs, each either in or out.
Number of relations $=2^6=64$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If the domain of the function $f(x)=\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2x-5}{11-3x}\right)+\sin^{-1}\left(2x^2-3x+1\right)$ is the interval $[\alpha, \beta]$, then $\alpha+2\beta$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$\sin^{-1}$ term: $-1\le 2x^2-3x+1\le 1$. The left inequality always holds; the right gives $x(2x-3)\le0$, i.e. $0\le x\le\dfrac32$.
On $\left[0,\dfrac32\right]$, $11-3x>0$, so $-1\le\dfrac{2x-5}{11-3x}\le1 \iff 3x-11\le 2x-5\le 11-3x \iff x\le6$ and $x\le\dfrac{16}{5}$, both true.
Domain $=\left[0,\dfrac32\right]$, so $\alpha+2\beta=0+3=3$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The sum of all the roots of the equation $(x-1)^2-5|x-1|+6=0$, is :
questions.sol:
Put $t=|x-1|\ge0$: $t^2-5t+6=0 \Rightarrow t=2$ or $3$.
$|x-1|=2 \Rightarrow x=3,-1$; $|x-1|=3 \Rightarrow x=4,-2$.
Sum $=3-1+4-2=4$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If $x^2+x+1=0$, then the value of $\left(x+\dfrac{1}{x}\right)^4+\left(x^2+\dfrac{1}{x^2}\right)^4+\left(x^3+\dfrac{1}{x^3}\right)^4+\ldots+\left(x^{25}+\dfrac{1}{x^{25}}\right)^4$ is :
questions.sol:
$x=\omega$ (a non-real cube root of unity), so $x^k+x^{-k}=\omega^k+\omega^{2k}$, which is $2$ if $3\mid k$ and $-1$ otherwise.
Fourth powers: $16$ when $3\mid k$, else $1$.
For $k=1,\ldots,25$ there are $8$ multiples of 3 and $17$ others.
Sum $=8(16)+17(1)=145$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots$ be a G.P. of increasing positive terms such that $a_2\cdot a_3\cdot a_4=64$ and $a_1+a_3+a_5=\dfrac{813}{7}$. Then $a_3+a_5+a_7$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$a_2a_3a_4=a_3^3=64 \Rightarrow a_3=4$. Let the common ratio be $r$ and $u=r^2$.
$a_1+a_3+a_5=4\left(\dfrac1u+1+u\right)=\dfrac{813}{7} \Rightarrow 28u^2-785u+28=0 \Rightarrow u=28$ or $\dfrac1{28}$.
Increasing terms, so $u=28$.
$a_3+a_5+a_7=4(1+u+u^2)=4(1+28+784)=3252$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The number of strictly increasing functions $f$ from the set $\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}$ to the set $\{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 9\}$ such that $f(i)\neq i$ for $1\le i\le 6$, is equal to :
questions.sol:
For a strictly increasing $f$ into $\{1,\ldots,9\}$, $i\le f(i)\le i+3$. Let $g(i)=f(i)-i$; then $g$ is non-decreasing with values in $\{0,1,2,3\}$.
$f(i)\neq i$ means $g(i)\ge1$, so $g$ is a non-decreasing sequence of length 6 from $\{1,2,3\}$.
Number of such sequences $=\binom{6+2}{2}=28$.

questions.text: Let the mean and variance of 7 observations $2, 4, 10, x, 12, 14, y$, $x>y$, be 8 and 16 respectively. Two numbers are chosen from $\{1, 2, 3, x-4, y, 5\}$ one after another without replacement, then the probability, that the smaller number among the two chosen numbers is less than 4, is :
questions.sol:
Sum $=56 \Rightarrow x+y=14$. $\sum x_i^2=7(16+64)=560 \Rightarrow x^2+y^2=560-460=100$.
So $xy=48$ and, with $x>y$, $x=8,\ y=6$.
The set is $\{1,2,3,4,6,5\}=\{1,\ldots,6\}$.
The smaller number is at least 4 only if both are from $\{4,5,6\}$: probability $\dfrac36\cdot\dfrac25=\dfrac15$.
Required probability $=1-\dfrac15=\dfrac45$.

questions.text: Let the foci of a hyperbola coincide with the foci of the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{36}+\dfrac{y^2}{16}=1$. If the eccentricity of the hyperbola is 5, then the length of its latus rectum is :
questions.sol:
Ellipse foci: $(\pm\sqrt{36-16},0)=(\pm2\sqrt5,0)$.
Hyperbola: $ae=2\sqrt5$ with $e=5$, so $a=\dfrac{2}{\sqrt5}$ and $b^2=a^2(e^2-1)=\dfrac45\cdot24=\dfrac{96}{5}$.
Latus rectum $=\dfrac{2b^2}{a}=\dfrac{192/5}{2/\sqrt5}=\dfrac{96}{\sqrt5}$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let a point A lie between the parallel lines $L_1$ and $L_2$ such that its distances from $L_1$ and $L_2$ are 6 and 3 units, respectively. Then the area (in sq. units) of the equilateral triangle ABC, where the points B and C lie on the lines $L_1$ and $L_2$, respectively, is :
questions.sol:
Take A at the origin, $L_1: y=6$, $L_2: y=-3$. Let AB make angle $\theta$ with the $x$-axis and AC angle $\theta-60^\circ$, side $s$.
$s\sin\theta=6$ and $s\sin(\theta-60^\circ)=-3$, so $\sin\theta=-2\sin(\theta-60^\circ)=-\sin\theta+\sqrt3\cos\theta \Rightarrow \tan\theta=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$.
Then $\sin\theta=\sqrt{\dfrac37}$ and $s^2=\dfrac{36}{3/7}=84$.
Area $=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4}\cdot84=21\sqrt3$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let PQ and MN be two straight lines touching the circle $x^2+y^2-4x-6y-3=0$ at the points A and B respectively. Let O be the centre of the circle and $\angle AOB=\pi/3$. Then the locus of the point of intersection of the lines PQ and MN is :
questions.sol:
Centre O$(2,3)$, radius $r=\sqrt{4+9+3}=4$.
If the tangents at A and B meet at T, then OT bisects $\angle AOB$, so $\angle AOT=\dfrac\pi6$ and $OT=\dfrac{r}{\cos(\pi/6)}=\dfrac{8}{\sqrt3}$.
Locus: $(x-2)^2+(y-3)^2=\dfrac{64}{3}$, i.e. $3(x^2+y^2)-12x-18y-25=0$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let O be the vertex of the parabola $x^2=4y$ and Q be any point on it. Let the locus of the point P, which divides the line segment OQ internally in the ratio $2:3$ be the conic C. Then the equation of the chord of C, which is bisected at the point $(1, 2)$, is :
questions.sol:
Q$=(2t,t^2)$, so P$=\dfrac25$Q$=\left(\dfrac{4t}{5},\dfrac{2t^2}{5}\right)$. Eliminating $t$: $x^2=\dfrac{8}{5}y$, i.e. $5x^2-8y=0$.
Chord with midpoint $(1,2)$: $T=S_1$, i.e. $5x\cdot1-4(y+2)=5-16$.
$5x-4y-8=-11 \Rightarrow 5x-4y+3=0$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The value of $\operatorname{cosec}10^\circ-\sqrt{3}\sec10^\circ$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{1}{\sin10^\circ}-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{\cos10^\circ}=\dfrac{\cos10^\circ-\sqrt3\sin10^\circ}{\sin10^\circ\cos10^\circ}=\dfrac{2\cos70^\circ}{\tfrac12\sin20^\circ}$.
Since $\cos70^\circ=\sin20^\circ$, the value is $4$.

questions.text: Let $(\alpha, \beta, \gamma)$ be the co-ordinates of the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the point $(5, 4, 2)$ on the line $\vec{r}=\left(-\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+\hat{k}\right)+\lambda\left(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-\hat{k}\right)$. Then the length of the projection of the vector $\alpha\hat{i}+\beta\hat{j}+\gamma\hat{k}$ on the vector $6\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ is :
questions.sol:
General point $(-1+2\lambda,\,3+3\lambda,\,1-\lambda)$; join to $(5,4,2)$: $(2\lambda-6,\,3\lambda-1,\,-\lambda-1)$.
Perpendicular to $(2,3,-1)$: $4\lambda-12+9\lambda-3+\lambda+1=0 \Rightarrow \lambda=1$, foot $(1,6,0)$.
Projection on $(6,2,3)$: $\dfrac{6+12+0}{7}=\dfrac{18}{7}$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $\vec{c}$ and $\vec{d}$ be vectors such that $\left|\vec{c}+\vec{d}\right|=\sqrt{29}$ and $\vec{c}\times\left(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\right)=\left(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\right)\times\vec{d}$. If $\lambda_1, \lambda_2$ $(\lambda_1>\lambda_2)$ are the possible values of $\left(\vec{c}+\vec{d}\right)\cdot\left(-7\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\right)$, then the equation $K^2x^2+\left(K^2-5K+\lambda_1\right)xy+\left(3K+\dfrac{\lambda_2}{2}\right)y^2-8x+12y+\lambda_2=0$ represents a circle, for K equal to :
questions.sol:
Let $\vec u=2\hat i+3\hat j+4\hat k$, $|\vec u|=\sqrt{29}$. The condition gives $(\vec c+\vec d)\times\vec u=\vec 0$, so $\vec c+\vec d=t\vec u$ with $|t|=1$.
$(\vec c+\vec d)\cdot(-7,2,3)=\pm(-14+6+12)=\pm4$, so $\lambda_1=4$, $\lambda_2=-4$.
Circle: $xy$ coefficient zero, $K^2-5K+4=0 \Rightarrow K=1,4$; equal $x^2$ and $y^2$ coefficients, $K^2=3K-2 \Rightarrow K=1,2$.
So $K=1$ (giving $x^2+y^2-8x+12y-4=0$, a real circle).
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $\vec{a}=-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$, $\vec{b}=8\hat{i}+7\hat{j}-3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c}$ be a vector such that $\vec{a}\times\vec{c}=\vec{b}$. If $\vec{c}\cdot\left(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\right)=4$, then $\left|\vec{a}+\vec{c}\right|^2$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Cross with $\vec a$: $\vec a\times(\vec a\times\vec c)=(\vec a\cdot\vec c)\vec a-9\vec c=\vec a\times\vec b=(-20,13,-23)$.
With $s=\vec a\cdot\vec c$: $\vec c=\dfrac{1}{9}\left(20-s,\ 2s-13,\ 2s+23\right)$.
$\vec c\cdot(1,1,1)=\dfrac{3s+30}{9}=4 \Rightarrow s=2$, so $\vec c=(2,-1,3)$.
$\vec a+\vec c=(1,1,5)$, $|\vec a+\vec c|^2=27$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The value of $\displaystyle\int_{-\pi/6}^{\pi/6}\left(\frac{\pi+4x^{11}}{1-\sin\left(|x|+\pi/6\right)}\right)dx$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
The denominator is even, so the $4x^{11}$ part integrates to $0$.
Remaining: $2\pi\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/6}\frac{dx}{1-\sin(x+\pi/6)}=2\pi\int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3}\frac{du}{1-\sin u}$.
$\displaystyle\int\frac{du}{1-\sin u}=\tan u+\sec u$, which is $\sqrt3+2$ at $\pi/3$ and $\sqrt3$ at $\pi/6$.
Value $=2\pi\cdot2=4\pi$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The area of the region, inside the ellipse $x^2+4y^2=4$ and outside the region bounded by the curves $y=|x|-1$ and $y=1-|x|$, is :
questions.sol:
Ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{4}+y^2=1$ has area $\pi\cdot2\cdot1=2\pi$.
The curves bound the square $|x|+|y|\le1$ with vertices $(\pm1,0),(0,\pm1)$, area $2$, which lies inside the ellipse.
Required area $=2\pi-2=2(\pi-1)$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution curve of the differential equation $(1+x^2)dy+\left(y-\tan^{-1}x\right)dx=0$, $y(0)=1$. Then the value of $y(1)$ is :
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{y}{1+x^2}=\dfrac{\tan^{-1}x}{1+x^2}$; integrating factor $e^{\tan^{-1}x}$.
With $t=\tan^{-1}x$: $ye^{t}=\displaystyle\int te^t\,dt=(t-1)e^t+C$, so $y=t-1+Ce^{-t}$.
$y(0)=1 \Rightarrow C=2$.
$y(1)=\dfrac\pi4-1+2e^{-\pi/4}=\dfrac{2}{e^{\pi/4}}+\dfrac\pi4-1$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $f:\mathbf{R}\to(0,\infty)$ be a twice differentiable function such that $f(3)=18$, $f'(3)=0$ and $f''(3)=4$. Then $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to1}\left(\log_e\left(\frac{f(2+x)}{f(3)}\right)^{\frac{18}{(x-1)^2}}\right)$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Let $h=x-1$ and $g=\log_e f$. The limit is $\displaystyle\lim_{h\to0}\frac{18\left[g(3+h)-g(3)\right]}{h^2}$.
$g'(3)=\dfrac{f'(3)}{f(3)}=0$ and $g''(3)=\dfrac{f''(3)f(3)-f'(3)^2}{f(3)^2}=\dfrac{4}{18}=\dfrac29$.
So $g(3+h)-g(3)\approx\dfrac{g''(3)}{2}h^2=\dfrac{h^2}{9}$ and the limit is $18\cdot\dfrac19=2$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: For some $\alpha, \beta\in\mathbf{R}$, let $A=\begin{bmatrix}\alpha&2\\1&2\end{bmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{bmatrix}1&1\\1&\beta\end{bmatrix}$ be such that $A^2-4A+2I=B^2-3B+I=O$. Then $\left(\det\left(\operatorname{adj}\left(A^3-B^3\right)\right)\right)^2$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
For a $2\times2$ matrix, $M^2-(\operatorname{tr}M)M+(\det M)I=O$. So $\alpha+2=4$, $\alpha=2$ ($\det A=2$ checks); $1+\beta=3$, $\beta=2$ ($\det B=1$ checks).
$A^3=4A^2-2A=14A-8I$ and $B^3=3B^2-B=8B-3I$.
$A^3-B^3=14A-8B-5I=\begin{bmatrix}15&20\\6&7\end{bmatrix}$, determinant $105-120=-15$.
For $2\times2$, $\det(\operatorname{adj}M)=\det M=-15$, and its square is $225$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $a_1=1$ and for $n\ge1$, $a_{n+1}=\dfrac{1}{2}a_n+\dfrac{n^2-2n-1}{n^2(n+1)^2}$. Then $\left|\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left(a_n-\frac{2}{n^2}\right)\right|$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Let $b_n=a_n-\dfrac{2}{n^2}$. Then $b_{n+1}=\dfrac12a_n+\dfrac{n^2-2n-1-2n^2}{n^2(n+1)^2}=\dfrac12a_n-\dfrac{(n+1)^2}{n^2(n+1)^2}=\dfrac12a_n-\dfrac1{n^2}=\dfrac12b_n$.
$b_1=1-2=-1$, so $b_n=-\left(\dfrac12\right)^{n-1}$.
$\sum b_n=-2$, and the absolute value is $2$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $S=\{(m, n): m, n\in\{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 50\}\}$. If the number of elements $(m, n)$ in S such that $6^m+9^n$ is a multiple of 5 is p and the number of elements $(m, n)$ in S such that $m+n$ is a square of a prime number is q, then $p+q$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Modulo 5: $6^m\equiv1$ and $9^n\equiv(-1)^n$, so $6^m+9^n\equiv0$ exactly when $n$ is odd: $p=50\times25=1250$.
$m+n\in[2,100]$ is a prime square for $m+n=4,9,25,49$; the number of pairs with sum $s\le51$ is $s-1$.
$q=3+8+24+48=83$.
$p+q=1333$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $f:\mathbf{R}\to\mathbf{R}$ be a twice differentiable function such that the quadratic equation $f(x)m^2-2f'(x)m+f''(x)=0$ in m, has two equal roots for every $x\in\mathbf{R}$. If $f(0)=1$, $f'(0)=2$, and $(\alpha, \beta)$ is the largest interval in which the function $f(\log_ex-x)$ is increasing, then $\alpha+\beta$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Equal roots: $4f'^2=4ff''$, so $\left(\dfrac{f'}{f}\right)'=\dfrac{ff''-f'^2}{f^2}=0$ and $\dfrac{f'}{f}$ is constant $=\dfrac{f'(0)}{f(0)}=2$. Hence $f(x)=e^{2x}$.
$f(\log_ex-x)=e^{2(\log_ex-x)}$ increases where $\log_ex-x$ does: $\dfrac1x-1>0 \iff 0<x<1$.
So $(\alpha,\beta)=(0,1)$ and $\alpha+\beta=1$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: $6\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi}\left|\left(\sin3x+\sin2x+\sin x\right)\right|dx$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
$\sin3x+\sin x=2\sin2x\cos x$, so the integrand is $|\sin2x\,(1+2\cos x)|$.
Sign: positive on $\left(0,\dfrac\pi2\right)$, negative on $\left(\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac{2\pi}3\right)$, positive on $\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3},\pi\right)$.
Antiderivative $F=-\dfrac{\cos2x}{2}-\dfrac{\cos3x}{3}-\cos x$: $F(0)=-\dfrac{11}{6}$, $F\left(\dfrac\pi2\right)=\dfrac12$, $F\left(\dfrac{2\pi}3\right)=\dfrac5{12}$, $F(\pi)=\dfrac56$.
Integral $=\dfrac{7}{3}+\dfrac{1}{12}+\dfrac{5}{12}=\dfrac{17}{6}$; times 6 gives $17$.

questions.text:
Consider a modified Bernoulli equation.
$\left(P+\dfrac{A}{Bt^2}\right)+\rho g(h+Bt)+\dfrac{1}{2}\rho V^2=\text{constant}$
If $t$ has the dimension of time then the dimensions of A and B are _______, _______ respectively.
questions.sol:
$Bt$ is added to the height $h$, so $[B]=\mathrm{LT^{-1}}$.
$\dfrac{A}{Bt^2}$ has the dimension of pressure: $[A]=\mathrm{ML^{-1}T^{-2}}\cdot\mathrm{LT^{-1}}\cdot\mathrm{T^2}=\mathrm{ML^0T^{-1}}$.
So A: $[\mathrm{ML^0T^{-1}}]$, B: $[\mathrm{M^0LT^{-1}}]$.

questions.text: Potential energy $(V)$ versus distance $(x)$ is given by the graph. Rank various regions as per the magnitudes of the force (F) acting on a particle from high to low.
questions.sol:
$|F|=\left|\dfrac{dV}{dx}\right|$, the magnitude of the slope of each segment.
AB: $1/1=1$; BC: $3/1=3$; CD: $0$; DE: $1/2=0.5$.
So $F_{BC}>F_{AB}>F_{DE}>F_{CD}$.

questions.text: A 4 kg mass moves under the influence of a force $\vec{F}=\left(4t^3\hat{i}-3t\hat{j}\right)$ N where $t$ is the time in second. If mass starts from origin at $t=0$, the velocity and position after $t=2$ s will be :
questions.sol:
$\vec a=\dfrac{\vec F}{4}=t^3\hat i-\dfrac{3t}{4}\hat j$ (starting from rest at the origin).
$\vec v=\dfrac{t^4}{4}\hat i-\dfrac{3t^2}{8}\hat j$; at $t=2$: $4\hat i-\dfrac32\hat j$.
$\vec r=\dfrac{t^5}{20}\hat i-\dfrac{t^3}{8}\hat j$; at $t=2$: $\dfrac85\hat i-\hat j$.

questions.text: An aluminium and steel rods having same lengths and cross-sections are joined to make total length of 120 cm at $30^\circ$C. The coefficient of linear expansion of aluminium and steel are $24\times10^{-6}/^\circ$C and $1.2\times10^{-5}/^\circ$C, respectively. The length of this composite rod when its temperature is raised to $100^\circ$C, is _______ cm.
questions.sol:
Each rod is 60 cm long and $\Delta T=70^\circ$C.
$\Delta L=60\times70\times(24+12)\times10^{-6}=0.1512$ cm.
New length $\approx120.15$ cm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Water flows through a horizontal tube as shown in the figure. The difference in height between the water columns in vertical tubes is 5 cm and the area of cross-sections at $A$ and $B$ are 6 cm$^2$ and 3 cm$^2$ respectively. The rate of flow will be _________ cm$^3$/s. (take $g=10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$)
questions.sol:
Continuity: $v_B=2v_A$. Bernoulli: $p_A-p_B=\dfrac12\rho(v_B^2-v_A^2)=\dfrac32\rho v_A^2=\rho gh$.
$v_A^2=\dfrac{2gh}{3}=\dfrac{2\times1000\times5}{3}\ \mathrm{cm^2/s^2}$ (using $g=1000$ cm/s$^2$), so $v_A=\dfrac{100}{\sqrt3}$ cm/s.
Rate of flow $=A_Av_A=6\times\dfrac{100}{\sqrt3}=200\sqrt3$ cm$^3$/s.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
The electric field in a plane electromagnetic wave is given by :
$E_y=69\sin[0.6\times10^3x-1.8\times10^{11}t]$ V/m.
The expression for magnetic field associated with this electromagnetic wave is __________ T.
questions.sol:
The phase $kx-\omega t$ shows travel along $+x$ (and $\omega/k=3\times10^8$ m/s).
$\vec E$ is along $y$, so $\vec B$ must be along $z$ (so that $\vec E\times\vec B$ points along $+x$), in phase with $\vec E$.
$B_0=\dfrac{E_0}{c}=\dfrac{69}{3\times10^8}=2.3\times10^{-7}$ T, giving $B_z=2.3\times10^{-7}\sin[0.6\times10^3x-1.8\times10^{11}t]$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two strings $(A, B)$ having linear densities $\mu_A=2\times10^{-4}$ kg/m and, $\mu_B=4\times10^{-4}$ kg/m and lengths $L_A=2.5$ m and $L_B=1.5$ m respectively are joined. Free ends of $A$ and $B$ are tied to two rigid supports $C$ and $D$, respectively creating a tension of 500 N in the wire. Two identical pulses, sent from $C$ and $D$ ends, take time $t_1$ and $t_2$, respectively, to reach the joint. The ratio $t_1/t_2$ is :
questions.sol:
Pulse speed $v=\sqrt{T/\mu}$, so the travel time is $t=L\sqrt{\mu/T}$.
$\dfrac{t_1}{t_2}=\dfrac{L_A}{L_B}\sqrt{\dfrac{\mu_A}{\mu_B}}=\dfrac{2.5}{1.5}\times\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\approx1.18$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Initially a satellite of 100 kg is in a circular orbit of radius $1.5R_E$. This satellite can be moved to a circular orbit of radius $3R_E$ by supplying $\alpha\times10^6$ J of energy The value of $\alpha$ is __________. (Take Radius of Earth $R_E=6\times10^6$ m and $g=10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$)
questions.sol:
Orbital energy $E=-\dfrac{GMm}{2r}=-\dfrac{gR_E^2m}{2r}$.
$\Delta E=\dfrac{gR_E^2m}{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{1.5R_E}-\dfrac{1}{3R_E}\right)=\dfrac{gR_Em}{6}$.
$=\dfrac{10\times6\times10^6\times100}{6}=10^9\ \mathrm{J}=1000\times10^6$ J, so $\alpha=1000$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A uniform rod of mass $m$ and length $l$ suspended by means of two identical inextensible light strings as shown in figure. Tension in one string immediately after the other string is cut, is __________. ($g$ acceleration due to gravity)
questions.sol:
Just after one string is cut, the rod starts to rotate about the other end (no velocity yet).
Torque about that end: $mg\dfrac l2=\dfrac{ml^2}{3}\alpha \Rightarrow \alpha=\dfrac{3g}{2l}$, so the centre accelerates down at $a=\alpha\dfrac l2=\dfrac{3g}{4}$.
$mg-T=m\cdot\dfrac{3g}{4} \Rightarrow T=\dfrac{mg}{4}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.text: A parallel plate capacitor has capacitance $C$, when there is vacuum within the parallel plates. A sheet having thickness $\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^{\text{rd}}$ of the separation between the plates and relative permittivity $K$ is introduced between the plates. The new capacitance of the system is :
questions.sol:
With a slab of thickness $t=d/3$: $C^\prime=\dfrac{\epsilon_0A}{d-t+t/K}=\dfrac{\epsilon_0A}{\dfrac{2d}{3}+\dfrac{d}{3K}}$.
$=\dfrac{\epsilon_0A}{d}\cdot\dfrac{3K}{2K+1}=\dfrac{3KC}{2K+1}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A current carrying solenoid is placed vertically and a particle of mass $m$ with charge $Q$ is released from rest. The particle moves along the axis of solenoid. If $g$ is acceleration due to gravity then the acceleration $(a)$ of the charged particle will satisfy :
questions.sol:
On the axis the magnetic field of the solenoid is along the axis, parallel to the velocity of the falling particle.
The magnetic force $Q\vec v\times\vec B$ is therefore zero, so only gravity acts: $a=g$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A conducting circular loop of area 1.0 m$^2$ is placed perpendicular to a magnetic field which varies as $B=\sin(100\,t)$ Tesla. If the resistance of the loop is 100 $\Omega$, then the average thermal energy dissipated in the loop in one period is __________ J.
questions.sol:
emf $\varepsilon=A\dfrac{dB}{dt}=100\cos(100t)$ V.
Mean power $=\dfrac{\varepsilon_0^2}{2R}=\dfrac{100^2}{200}=50$ W.
One period $T=\dfrac{2\pi}{100}$ s, so energy $=50\times\dfrac{2\pi}{100}=\pi$ J.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A 1 m long metal rod AB completes the circuit as shown in figure. The area of circuit is perpendicular to the magnetic field of 0.10 T. If the resistance of the total circuit is 2 $\Omega$ then the force needed to move the rod towards right with constant speed $(v)$ of 1.5 m/s is _________N.
questions.sol:
Motional emf $\varepsilon=Blv=0.1\times1\times1.5=0.15$ V; current $I=\dfrac{0.15}{2}=0.075$ A.
At constant speed the applied force balances the magnetic force: $F=BIl=0.1\times0.075\times1=7.5\times10^{-3}$ N.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In a double slit experiment the distance between the slits is 0.1 cm and the screen is placed at 50 cm from the slits plane. When one slit is covered with a transparent sheet having thickness $t$ and refractive index $n(=1.5)$, the central fringe shifts by 0.2 cm. The value of $t$ is __________ cm.
questions.sol:
Fringe shift $y=\dfrac{(n-1)tD}{d}$.
$0.2=\dfrac{0.5\times t\times50}{0.1}=250t \Rightarrow t=8\times10^{-4}$ cm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A light wave described by $E=60[\sin(3\times10^{15})t+\sin(12\times10^{15})t]$ (in SI units) falls on a metal surface of work function 2.8 eV. The maximum kinetic energy of ejected photoelectron is (approximately) _________ eV. ($h=6.6\times10^{-34}$ J.s. and $e=1.6\times10^{-19}$ C)
questions.sol:
The higher angular frequency is $\omega=12\times10^{15}$ rad/s, so $\nu=\dfrac{\omega}{2\pi}\approx1.91\times10^{15}$ Hz.
Photon energy $h\nu=\dfrac{6.6\times10^{-34}\times1.91\times10^{15}}{1.6\times10^{-19}}\approx7.9$ eV.
$K_{max}\approx7.9-2.8\approx5.1$ eV.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text: If an alpha particle with energy 7.7 MeV is bombarded on a thin gold foil, the closest distance from nucleus it can reach is _________m. (Atomic number of gold $=79$ and $\dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_o}=9\times10^9$ in SI units)
questions.sol:
At closest approach, $K=\dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\dfrac{(2e)(79e)}{r_0}$.
$r_0=\dfrac{9\times10^9\times158\times(1.6\times10^{-19})^2}{7.7\times10^6\times1.6\times10^{-19}}=\dfrac{9\times10^9\times158\times1.6\times10^{-19}}{7.7\times10^6}\approx2.95\times10^{-14}$ m.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A gas based geyser heats water flowing at the rate of 5.0 litres per minute from $27^\circ$C to $87^\circ$C. The rate of consumption of the gas is _________g/s.
(Take heat of combustion of gas $=5.0\times10^4$ J/g) specific heat capacity of water $=4200$ J/kg.$^\circ$C
questions.sol:
Mass flow $=5$ kg/min $=\dfrac{1}{12}$ kg/s.
Heat needed per second $=\dfrac{1}{12}\times4200\times60=21000$ J/s.
Gas used $=\dfrac{21000}{5\times10^4}=0.42$ g/s.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The given circuit works as :
questions.sol:
Each input first passes through a NOT gate, giving $\bar A$ and $\bar B$.
The middle gate is a NOR: output $\overline{\bar A+\bar B}=AB$.
The last NOT gate gives $\overline{AB}$, so the circuit is a NAND gate.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A point charge of $10^{-8}$ C is placed at origin. The work done in moving a point charge 2 $\mu$C from point $A(4, 4, 2)$ m to $B(2, 2, 1)$ m is __________ J. ($\dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_o}=9\times10^9$ in SI units)
questions.sol:
$r_A=\sqrt{16+16+4}=6$ m, $r_B=\sqrt{4+4+1}=3$ m.
$W=q(V_B-V_A)=2\times10^{-6}\times9\times10^9\times10^{-8}\left(\dfrac13-\dfrac16\right)$.
$=2\times10^{-6}\times90\times\dfrac16=30\times10^{-6}$ J.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In an experiment the values of two spring constants were measured as $k_1=(10\pm0.2)$ N/m and $k_2=(20\pm0.3)$ N/m. If these springs are connected in parallel, then the percentage error in equivalent spring constant is :
questions.sol:
In parallel, $k=k_1+k_2=30$ N/m and the absolute errors add: $\Delta k=0.2+0.3=0.5$ N/m.
Percentage error $=\dfrac{0.5}{30}\times100\approx1.67\%$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two identical thin rods of mass $M$ kg and length $L$ m are connected as shown in figure. Moment of inertia of the combined rod system about an axis passing through point $P$ and perpendicular to the plane of the rods is $\dfrac{x}{12}ML^2$ kg m$^2$. The value of $x$ is __________.
questions.sol:
Vertical rod about its end P: $\dfrac{ML^2}{3}=\dfrac{4}{12}ML^2$.
Horizontal rod: its centre is at distance $L$ from P, so $\dfrac{ML^2}{12}+ML^2=\dfrac{13}{12}ML^2$.
Total $=\dfrac{17}{12}ML^2$, so $x=17$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.text: A collimated beam of light of diameter 2 mm is propagating along $x$-axis. The beam is required to be expanded in a collimated beam of diameter 14 mm using a system of two convex lenses. If first lens has focal length 40 mm, then the focal length of second lens is __________ mm.
questions.sol:
Two convex lenses separated by $f_1+f_2$ (common focus) keep the beam parallel.
By similar triangles, the beam diameter scales by $\dfrac{f_2}{f_1}$: $\dfrac{f_2}{40}=\dfrac{14}{2}=7$.
$f_2=280$ mm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In a microscope the objective is having focal length $f_o=2$ cm and eye-piece is having focal length $f_e=4$ cm. The tube length is 32 cm. The magnification produced by this microscope for normal adjustment is __________.
questions.sol:
For normal adjustment (final image at infinity), $m=\dfrac{L}{f_o}\cdot\dfrac{D}{f_e}$ with $D=25$ cm.
$m=\dfrac{32}{2}\times\dfrac{25}{4}=16\times6.25=100$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The heat generated in 1 minute between points $A$ and $B$ in the given circuit, when a battery of 9 V with internal resistance of 1 $\Omega$ is connected across these points is __________ J.
questions.sol:
The network is a balanced Wheatstone bridge ($\dfrac12=\dfrac24$), so the middle 1 $\Omega$ carries no current.
Branches: $1+2=3\ \Omega$ and $2+4=6\ \Omega$ in parallel, giving $2\ \Omega$ between A and B.
Current $I=\dfrac{9}{2+1}=3$ A; heat in 60 s $=I^2Rt=9\times2\times60=1080$ J.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: 10 mole of oxygen is heated at constant volume from $30^\circ$C to $40^\circ$C. The change in the internal energy of the gas is __________ cal. (The molecular specific heat of oxygen at constant pressure, $C_p=7$ cal/mol.$^\circ$C and $R=2$ cal./mol.$^\circ$C.)
questions.sol:
$C_v=C_p-R=5$ cal/mol $^\circ$C.
$\Delta U=nC_v\Delta T=10\times5\times10=500$ cal.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: 80 mL of a hydrocarbon on mixing with 264 mL of oxygen in a closed U-tube undergoes complete combustion. The residual gases after cooling to 273 K occupy 224 mL. When the system is treated with KOH solution, the volume decreases to 64 mL. The formula of the hydrocarbon is :
questions.sol:
KOH absorbs $\mathrm{CO_2}$: $224-64=160$ mL, and the remaining 64 mL is unused $\mathrm{O_2}$ (water has condensed).
$\mathrm{C_xH_y+\left(x+\tfrac y4\right)O_2\rightarrow xCO_2+\tfrac y2H_2O}$: $80x=160 \Rightarrow x=2$.
$\mathrm{O_2}$ used $=264-64=200=80\left(2+\dfrac y4\right) \Rightarrow y=2$.
The hydrocarbon is $\mathrm{C_2H_2}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
14.0 g of calcium metal is allowed to react with excess HCl at 1.0 atm pressure and 273 K. Which of the following statements is incorrect ?
[Given : Molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ of Ca-40, Cl-35.5, H-1]
options: The limiting reagent is calcium metal.
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{Ca+2HCl\rightarrow CaCl_2+H_2}$; moles of Ca $=\dfrac{14}{40}=0.35$, and Ca is limiting since HCl is in excess.
$\mathrm{H_2}$: 0.35 mol $=0.35\times22.4=7.84$ L at STP.
$\mathrm{CaCl_2}$: $0.35\times111=38.85$ g, not 33.3 g, so that statement is incorrect.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I :
The number of species among $\mathrm{SF_4}$, $\mathrm{NH_4^+}$, $\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}}$, $\mathrm{XeF_4}$, $\mathrm{[PtCl_4]^{2-}}$, $\mathrm{SeF_4}$ and $\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}$, that have tetrahedral geometry is 3.
Statement II :
In the set $\mathrm{[NO_2, BeH_2, BF_3, AlCl_3]}$, all the molecules have incomplete octet around central atom.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Tetrahedral: $\mathrm{NH_4^+}$ and $\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}}$ only. $\mathrm{SF_4}$, $\mathrm{SeF_4}$ are see-saw; $\mathrm{XeF_4}$, $\mathrm{[PtCl_4]^{2-}}$, $\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}$ are square planar. The count is 2, so Statement I is false.
$\mathrm{NO_2}$ (odd electron, 7 around N), $\mathrm{BeH_2}$ (4), $\mathrm{BF_3}$ and $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$ (6) all have fewer than 8 electrons around the central atom, so Statement II is true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : When an electric discharge is passed through gaseous hydrogen, the hydrogen molecules dissociate and the energetically excited hydrogen atoms produce electromagnetic radiation of discrete frequencies.
Statement II : The frequency of second line of Balmer series obtained from $\mathrm{He^+}$ is equal to that of first line of Lyman series obtained from hydrogen atom.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I describes the origin of the hydrogen line spectrum correctly.
$\mathrm{He^+}$ ($Z=2$), second Balmer line ($4\to2$): $\bar\nu\propto4\left(\dfrac14-\dfrac1{16}\right)=\dfrac34$.
H, first Lyman line ($2\to1$): $\bar\nu\propto1-\dfrac14=\dfrac34$. They are equal, so both statements are true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
For the reaction, $\mathrm{N_2O_4\rightleftharpoons2NO_2}$, graph is plotted as shown below. Identify correct statements.
A. Standard free energy change for the reaction is $-5.40$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.
B. As $\Delta G^\ominus$ in graph is positive, $\mathrm{N_2O_4}$ will not dissociate into $\mathrm{NO_2}$ at all.
C. Reverse reaction will go to completion.
D. When 1 mole of $\mathrm{N_2O_4}$ changes into equilibrium mixture, value of $\Delta G^\ominus=-0.84$ kJ mol$^{-1}$
E. When 2 mole of $\mathrm{NO_2}$ changes into equilibrium mixture, $\Delta G^\ominus$ for equilibrium mixture is $-6.24$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
From the graph, pure $\mathrm{N_2O_4}$ (A) to pure $\mathrm{NO_2}$ (B) is $+5.40$ kJ mol$^{-1}$, so A is false.
A positive $\Delta G^\ominus$ only means $K<1$; some dissociation still happens and the minimum E is the equilibrium mixture, so B and C are false.
A to E: $G$ falls by 0.84, so D is true. B to E: $G$ falls by $5.40+0.84=6.24$, so E is true.
Answer: D and E only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Which of the following graphs between pressure 'p' versus volume 'V' represents the maximum work done ?
questions.sol:
Work is the area under the p-V path (net area for a cycle).
(4): constant pressure 2.0 bar from 0 to 22.4 L, area $=2.0\times22.4=44.8$ L bar, the largest.
(3): the curve from (22.4 L, 2.0 bar) to (44.8 L, 1.0 bar) encloses less (between 22.4 and 44.8 L bar). The cycles (1) and (2) only give the small enclosed areas.
So graph (4) shows the maximum work.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Elements P and Q form two types of non-volatile, non-ionizable compounds PQ and $\mathrm{PQ_2}$. When 1 g of PQ is dissolved in 50 g of solvent 'A', $\Delta T_b$ was 1.176 K while when 1 g of $\mathrm{PQ_2}$ is dissolved in 50 g of solvent 'A', $\Delta T_b$ was 0.689 K. ($K_b$ of 'A' $=5$ K kg mol$^{-1}$). The molar masses of elements P and Q (in g mol$^{-1}$) respectively, are :
questions.sol:
$M=\dfrac{K_b\times w\times1000}{\Delta T_b\times W}$.
PQ: $M=\dfrac{5\times1\times1000}{1.176\times50}\approx85$; $\mathrm{PQ_2}$: $M=\dfrac{5000}{0.689\times50}\approx145$.
$Q=145-85=60$ and $P=85-60=25$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Which of the following represents the correct trend for the mentioned property ?
A. F > P > S > B - First Ionization Energy
B. Cl > F > S > P - Electron Affinity
C. K > Al > Mg > B - Metallic character
D. $\mathrm{K_2O>Na_2O>MgO>Al_2O_3}$ - Basic character
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A: F (1681) > P (1012) > S (1000) > B (801 kJ mol$^{-1}$): correct (P exceeds S because of its half-filled 3p).
B: electron gain enthalpy magnitude Cl > F > S > P: correct.
C: Mg is more metallic than Al, so K > Al > Mg > B is wrong.
D: basic character falls from $\mathrm{K_2O}$ to amphoteric $\mathrm{Al_2O_3}$: correct.
Answer: A, B and D only.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : The number of pairs among $\mathrm{[SiO_2, CO_2]}$, $\mathrm{[SnO, SnO_2]}$, $\mathrm{[PbO, PbO_2]}$ and $\mathrm{[GeO, GeO_2]}$, which contain oxides that are both amphoteric is 2.
Statement II : $\mathrm{BF_3}$ is an electron deficient molecule, can act as a Lewis acid, forms adduct with $\mathrm{NH_3}$ and has a trigonal planar geometry.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{SiO_2}$, $\mathrm{CO_2}$ are acidic; $\mathrm{GeO_2}$ is acidic. $\mathrm{SnO}$, $\mathrm{SnO_2}$, $\mathrm{PbO}$, $\mathrm{PbO_2}$ are all amphoteric. So exactly 2 pairs qualify and Statement I is true.
$\mathrm{BF_3}$ has only 6 electrons on B ($sp^2$, trigonal planar), accepts a lone pair and forms $\mathrm{F_3B\leftarrow NH_3}$. Statement II is true.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text: $\mathrm{MnO_4^{2-}}$, in acidic medium, disproportionates to :
questions.sol:
Manganate (Mn +6) is unstable in acid: $\mathrm{3MnO_4^{2-}+4H^+\rightarrow2MnO_4^-+MnO_2+2H_2O}$.
Mn goes up to +7 ($\mathrm{MnO_4^-}$) and down to +4 ($\mathrm{MnO_2}$).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Among $\mathrm{[Cu(NH_3)_4]^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{[Ni(en)_3)]^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{[Ni(NH_3)_6]^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{[Mn(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{[Mn(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}$ has the maximum number of unpaired electrons.
Statement II : The number of pairs among $\mathrm{\{[NiCl_4]^{2-}, [Ni(CO)_4]\}}$, $\mathrm{\{[NiCl_4]^{2-}, [Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}\}}$ and $\mathrm{\{[Ni(CO)_4], [Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}\}}$ that contain only diamagnetic species is two.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Unpaired electrons: $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ ($d^9$) 1; $\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}$ ($d^8$, octahedral) 2 in both Ni complexes; $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}$ ($d^5$, weak field $\mathrm{H_2O}$) 5. Statement I is true.
$\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}}$ (tetrahedral $d^8$) is paramagnetic; $\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_4]}$ ($d^{10}$) and $\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}$ (square planar $d^8$) are diamagnetic.
Only the third pair is fully diamagnetic, so the count is one and Statement II is false.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: In Carius method, 0.75 g of an organic compound gave 1.2 g of barium sulphate, find percentage of sulphur (molar mass 32 g mol$^{-1}$). Molar mass of barium sulphate is 233 g mol$^{-1}$.
questions.sol:
Mass of S $=\dfrac{32}{233}\times1.2$ g.
%S $=\dfrac{32\times1.2}{233\times0.75}\times100=\dfrac{38.4}{174.75}\times100\approx21.97\%$.

questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text: From the following, the least stable structure is :
questions.sol:
These are charge-separated resonance forms of 1-nitrobutadiene-type structures.
In structure (4) the positive charge on carbon sits directly next to the positively charged N of the nitro group: like charges on adjacent atoms strongly destabilise a structure.
Hence (4) is the least stable.

questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text:
Identify correct statements from the following :
A. Propanal and propanone are functional isomers.
B. Ethoxyethane and methoxypropane are metamers.
C. But-2-ene shows optical isomerism.
D. But-1-ene and but-2-ene are functional isomers.
E. Pentane and 2, 2-dimethyl propane are chain isomers.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A: aldehyde vs ketone of $\mathrm{C_3H_6O}$, functional isomers: true.
B: same ether group, different alkyl groups on O: metamers, true.
C: but-2-ene has no chiral centre (it shows geometrical isomerism): false.
D: both are alkenes, differing in the position of C=C (position isomers): false.
E: different carbon chains of $\mathrm{C_5H_{12}}$: chain isomers, true.
Answer: A, B and E only.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text: A hydrocarbon 'P' $(\mathrm{C_4H_8})$ on reaction with HCl gives an optically active compound 'Q' $(\mathrm{C_4H_9Cl})$ which on reaction with one mole of ammonia gives compound 'R' $(\mathrm{C_4H_{11}N})$. 'R' on diazotization followed by hydrolysis gives 'S'. Identify P, Q, R and S.
questions.sol:
Q is optically active, so the Cl is on C-2: Q $=\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH(Cl)CH_3}$ (2-chlorobutane), formed from but-2-ene (P) by HCl addition.
Ammonolysis gives butan-2-amine (R), $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH(NH_2)CH_3}$.
Nitrous acid on this primary amine followed by hydrolysis gives butan-2-ol (S).
This is option (2).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Identify A in the following reaction.
questions.sol:
Adding $2\mathrm{H_2}$ gives decalin, so A is a bicyclic $\mathrm{C_{10}}$ compound with two C=C bonds.
Hot $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ gives cyclohexane-1,2-dicarboxylic acid and oxalic acid: one ring is untouched, and the other is cut at two C=C bonds into two COOH groups on the ring-fusion carbons plus a $\mathrm{C_2}$ fragment.
So both double bonds lie in one ring as C1=C2 and C3=C4, away from the fusion carbons, which is structure (4).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: An organic compound "P" of molecular formula $\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_3}$ gives positive Iodoform test but negative Tollen's test. When "P" is treated with dilute acid, it produces "Q". "Q" gives positive Tollen's test and also iodoform test. The structure of "P" is :
questions.sol:
P has a methyl ketone ($\mathrm{CH_3CO-}$, iodoform positive) and no free CHO (Tollens negative); acid releases an aldehyde, so P contains an acetal $\mathrm{-CH(OCH_3)_2}$.
Structure (3), $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_2CH(OCH_3)_2}$ ($\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_3}$), hydrolyses to $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_2CHO}$, which gives both tests.
(4) already has a free CHO; (1) and (2) are ethers that give no aldehyde on hydrolysis.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: An organic compound (P) on treatment with aqueous ammonia under hot condition forms compound (Q) which on heating with $\mathrm{Br_2}$ and KOH forms compound (R) having molecular formula $\mathrm{C_6H_7N}$. Names of P, Q and R respectively are.
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{C_6H_7N}$ is aniline, $\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2}$.
Hofmann bromamide degradation removes one carbon: Q is benzamide, $\mathrm{C_6H_5CONH_2}$.
Benzamide comes from benzoic acid with ammonia on heating, so P is benzoic acid.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Identify the correct statements.
A. Arginine and Tryptophan are essential amino acids.
B. Histidine does not contain heterocyclic ring in its structure.
C. Proline is a six membered cyclic ring amino acid.
D. Glycine does not have chiral centre.
E. Cysteine has characteristic feature of side chain as $\mathrm{MeS-CH_2-CH_2-}$.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A: both are listed as essential amino acids: true.
B: histidine has an imidazole ring: false.
C: proline has a five-membered (pyrrolidine) ring: false.
D: glycine ($\mathrm{H_2NCH_2COOH}$) has no chiral carbon: true.
E: $\mathrm{CH_3S-CH_2CH_2-}$ is the side chain of methionine; cysteine has $\mathrm{HS-CH_2-}$: false.
Answer: A and D only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following reactions.
$\mathrm{PbCl_2+K_2CrO_4\rightarrow A+2KCl}$
(Hot solution)
$\mathrm{A+NaOH\rightleftharpoons B+Na_2CrO_4}$
$\mathrm{PbSO_4+4CH_3COONH_4\rightarrow(NH_4)_2SO_4+X}$
In the above reactions, A, B and X are respectively.
questions.sol:
Hot $\mathrm{PbCl_2}$ with chromate gives yellow lead chromate: A $=\mathrm{PbCrO_4}$.
$\mathrm{PbCrO_4}$ dissolves in NaOH as plumbite: B $=\mathrm{Na_2[Pb(OH)_4]}$.
$\mathrm{PbSO_4}$ dissolves in ammonium acetate as the acetato complex: X $=\mathrm{(NH_4)_2[Pb(CH_3COO)_4]}$.
This is option (2).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following reaction sequence
The percentage of nitrogen in product 'T' formed is _________%. (Nearest integer)
(Given molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ H : 1, C : 12, N : 14, O : 16)
questions.sol:
P = nitrobenzene; Sn/HCl then neutralisation gives aniline (Q); acetic anhydride gives acetanilide (R).
Nitration of acetanilide gives mainly 4-nitroacetanilide (S); acid hydrolysis then neutralisation gives 4-nitroaniline (T), $\mathrm{C_6H_6N_2O_2}$, $M=138$.
%N $=\dfrac{28}{138}\times100\approx20.3$, so 20.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following reactions :
$\mathrm{NaCl+K_2Cr_2O_7+H_2SO_4\rightarrow A+KHSO_4+NaHSO_4+H_2O}$
$\mathrm{A+NaOH\rightarrow B+NaCl+H_2O}$
$\mathrm{B+H_2SO_4+H_2O_2\rightarrow C+Na_2SO_4+H_2O}$
In the product 'C', 'X' is the number of $\mathrm{O_2^{2-}}$ units, 'Y' is the total number oxygen atoms present and 'Z' is the oxidation state of Cr. The value of X+Y+Z is __________.
questions.sol:
A is chromyl chloride, $\mathrm{CrO_2Cl_2}$; with NaOH it gives sodium chromate, B $=\mathrm{Na_2CrO_4}$.
Acidified $\mathrm{H_2O_2}$ converts chromate into chromium peroxide, C $=\mathrm{CrO_5}$ (one Cr=O and two peroxo groups).
X $=2$, Y $=5$, Z $=+6$, so X+Y+Z $=13$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Use the following data :
Substance$\Delta_fH^\ominus$ (500K) / kJ mol$^{-1}$$S^\ominus$ (500K) / J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$
AB(g)32222
$\mathrm{A_2(g)}$6146
$\mathrm{B_2(g)}$$x$280
One mole each of $\mathrm{A_2(g)}$ and $\mathrm{B_2(g)}$ are taken in a 1 L closed flask and allowed to establish the equilibrium at 500K.
$\mathrm{A_2(g)+B_2(g)\rightleftharpoons2AB(g)}$
The value of $x$ (in kJ mol$^{-1}$) is __________. (Nearest integer)
(Given : log K = 2.2 R = 8.3 J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$)

questions.text:
The pH and conductance of a weak acid (HX) was found to be 5 and $4\times10^{-5}$ S, respectively. The conductance was measured under standard condition using a cell where the electrode plates having a surface area of 1 cm$^2$ were at a distance of 15 cm apart. The value of the limiting molar conductivity is __________ S m$^2$ mol$^{-1}$. (nearest integer)
(Given : degree of dissociation of the weak acid $(\alpha)$ << 1)
questions.sol:
Conductivity $\kappa=G\dfrac{l}{A}=4\times10^{-5}\times\dfrac{15}{1}=6\times10^{-4}$ S cm$^{-1}=6\times10^{-2}$ S m$^{-1}$.
$\Lambda_m=\dfrac{\kappa}{c}$ and $\alpha=\dfrac{\Lambda_m}{\Lambda_m^\circ}$, so $\Lambda_m^\circ=\dfrac{\kappa}{c\alpha}=\dfrac{\kappa}{[\mathrm{H^+}]}$.
$[\mathrm{H^+}]=10^{-5}$ mol L$^{-1}=10^{-2}$ mol m$^{-3}$, so $\Lambda_m^\circ=\dfrac{6\times10^{-2}}{10^{-2}}=6$ S m$^2$ mol$^{-1}$.

questions.text: Pre-exponential factors of two different reactions of same order are identical. Let activation energy of first reaction exceeds the activation energy of second reaction by 20 kJ mol$^{-1}$. If $k_1$ and $k_2$ are the rate constants of first and second reaction respectively at 300 K, then $\ln\dfrac{k_2}{k_1}$ will be __________. (nearest integer) [$R=8.3$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$]
questions.sol:
$k=Ae^{-E_a/RT}$ with the same $A$, so $\ln\dfrac{k_2}{k_1}=\dfrac{E_{a1}-E_{a2}}{RT}$.
$=\dfrac{20000}{8.3\times300}\approx8.03$, so 8.
